title: Rabbi Yirmeyah son of Shalom
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Midrash Mishlei, beginning of chapter 1, and in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 3, end of halakhah 1: ‘Rabbi Yirmeyah bar ר״ש said.’ Perhaps this means son of R' Shalom; in the Venice printing, however, it explicitly reads ‘bar Shimon.’

notes.text: ר״ש could be read in more than one way: Hyman proposes Shalom, but reports that the Venice printing explicitly has Shimon.

The saved whole Buber MidrashMishlei1 opening scalar explicitly names Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Shalom; whole Venice JerusalemTalmudShabbat3:1 scalar12 has Rabbi Yirmeyah bei Rabbi Shimon. These supersede the earlier Shabbat nonmatch, but do not prove Hyman’s printed edition or whether this scalar is at the end of the halakhah. Supplied bar and named bei remain distinct. Hyman’s perhaps son of R' Shalom is tentative, not a newly proved expansion of ר״ש; no full title for that proposed Shalom father is supplied. רפ״א means beginning of chapter1, not81.

Midrash Mishlei 1 names Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Shalom. The digital Venice text of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:1 spells out Yirmeyah bei Rabbi Shimon in the next-to-last paragraph of that halakhah. Hyman’s printed notice reports bar Shimon and separately suggests Shalom for the abbreviated ר״ש.
